sentences.text: A retrospective cohort study assessed 197 stroke survivors at a median of 386 days after their event to examine medication adherence patterns.
While 79% of participants reported high medication adherence, many did not understand the reason for taking their drugs.
No significant differences in medication adherence were found between different ethnicities or sexes.

Longer hospital stays, greater post-stroke disability, and caregiver involvement were associated with high medication adherence, whereas the lowest levels were observed in patients who had mild strokes.
